inputs.original_text: Micheál Martin can point to more tenancies, but that statistic means little if people are still being pushed out of their homes. Eviction notices, homelessness and the number of people in emergency accommodation are all rising. The six-year lease rules introduced on March 1 are being discussed against that backdrop, but a housing system that leaves people without secure homes is failing them. We should judge policy by whether renters—especially those most vulnerable to displacement—can stay housed, not by headline figures that hide their insecurity.
inputs.modified_text: More tenancies mean little when renters are still being forced from their homes. Rising eviction notices, homelessness and emergency accommodation point to a system that protects insecurity rather than people. The six-year lease rules introduced on March 1 should be judged by whether they give renters—especially those most vulnerable to displacement—real security, not by headline figures that make the housing crisis look better than it is.
